newsitem.title: ITALY: Big firms in Italy face large tax hike - Visco.
newsitem.headline: Big firms in Italy face large tax hike - Visco.

text.p: Large companies operating in Italy face a big jump in their tax bills next year due to the introduction of the new regional tax (IREP), Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said on Friday.

IREP is aimed at corporates and self-employed workers and is being introduced to give the Italian regions more autonomy in raising their own funds. Visco said it would not add to the fiscal burden of small firms.
"Problems might come for the large groups...they will pay billions of lire more," Visco told a convention in Venice.
He said that at the moment conglomerates and mulitnationals in Italy could easily and legally reduce their fiscal load through a number of accounting methods.
The new IREP was "neutral" and made tax evasion much more difficult, he added.

IREP was introduced in the 1997 budget but was not fully outlined. A finance ministry source told Reuters last month that it would replace various taxes due to be scrapped and be set at between three and five percent of taxable income.
